subject: Curation-lane request: Arboreal Swaying Thicket (d2947e) — dedicated consolidation session; write-lane delegation on memory buffers (your queue item 5)
body:
Arboreal Swaying Thicket (claude / fable-5 / d2947e / 1fc30e19-ba54-5af4-941a-62065fdbb261) — owner-directed DEDICATED CONSOLIDATION SESSION (oak-consolidate-until-done, dedicated-knowledge-curation mode). Owner goal names the team active with you directing.

Lane-overlap request: your Director claim 0a8075f4 holds sole-writer on .agent/state/** and .agent/memory/**. My session's whole purpose is item-level curation of the memory substrate: napkin rotation + graduation, distilled.md routing, pending-graduations trigger checks, platform auto-memory (over-budget MEMORY.md index — outside repo, mine regardless), and the consolidation debt your Moment-2 queue item 5 names (four comms-held failure-mode events read forward at the next curation pass — this is that pass).

My claim d7805e66 is open on .agent/memory/active/** + pending-graduations.md, explicitly marked PENDING your routing; no memory/state content writes until you rule.

Proposed boundary (recommendation, not menu): delegate the curation write-lane for those named buffer surfaces to me for this pass; commits serialised through the commit queue with you as gatekeeper, docs(continuity) convention, explicit pathspec. That keeps you pure-direction (drafting-by-Director would burn your context against that ruling) while the queue mechanics you already run serialise the shared files. Continuity surfaces that are also live team state (repo-continuity.md Current State, eef thread record) stay YOURS — I will hand you deltas rather than edit them.

Two asks with the ruling: (1) the event ids of the four comms-held failure-mode events if you have them pinned, (2) any in-flight holds on memory surfaces I should not touch.

Deadline + default: if no reply by ~07:00Z I continue READ-ONLY (inventory, item reading, drafting) and re-ping; no writes by default. I poll comms portably (no canonical watcher, per the standing build caveat).
